subject: Distribution & licensing for OpenWeights model family — partnership terms
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karen Lee <karen@openweights.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom@boldconsulting.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0000
Subject: Distribution & licensing for OpenWeights model family — partnership terms

Hi Karen and Tom,

Thanks again for the productive conversation last week. As discussed, Redwood is interested in distributing and serving OpenWeights' smaller and mid-tier models through three channels: (1) hosted inference (Redwood hosted API), (2) Dedicated pools for enterprise customers, and (3) Private deployments (VPC / on-prem bundles we deliver to customers).

High level asks / constraints from our side:
- Ability to host quantized weights for inference in our hosted environment (we use 4-bit/8-bit quantization and require clarification on redistribution of quantized artifacts).
- A distribution license that permits serving models to end-customers (not redistribution of raw weights to customers) across the three deployment modes.
- Clear terms for research/benchmarking, eval sets, and allowed use cases (safety/filtered uses).
- Revenue share / commercial terms and any minimum guarantees you expect.

Can you share your standard distribution/master publisher agreement and any non-commercial licensing carve-outs for the models we discussed? If you can attach the current MPA, we’ll circulate an internal redline and propose a technical integration checklist for engineering.

Proposed next step: legal + engineering sync next week to go over the MPA and any technical constraints around quantized weights & caching. We’d like to keep timeline tight: pilot with a single mid-tier model by end of Q2 if possible.

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Karen Lee <karen@openweights.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@boldconsulting.com>
Cc: legal@openweights.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Distribution & licensing for OpenWeights model family — partnership terms

Marissa — thanks, and great to continue the thread.

Attaching our current Master Publishing Agreement (MPA) and a short appendix that outlines permitted/forbidden redistribution for different weight artifacts. Short summary of the key points you should expect in the doc:
- We license model weights under two tracks: (A) "Hosted Serving License" for vendors who host the model and provide inference-as-a-service, and (B) "Redistribution License" for partners who ship raw weights to third parties (rare / special approval).
- Quantized weights: we generally allow hosting of quantized artifacts under the Hosted Serving License but require a quantization-usage appendix and a technical attestation that quantization steps do not enable reconstitution of full-precision weights for downstream redistribution.
- Security/supply-chain controls: customers with Dedicated/Private deployments may require a signed addendum for on-prem shipping; we accept encrypted container handoffs under strict custody rules.
- Commercial terms: revenue share baseline is 20% to publisher for hosted revenue; redistribution licenses are priced case-by-case.

See attached: OpenWeights_Master_Distribution_Terms_v1.pdf (MPA) and an internal note for your legal team. Tom from Bold has been helping coordinate the commercial model — appreciate his help there.

Karen Lee
Head of Partnerships, OpenWeights Inc.
karen@openweights.ai
+1 (206) 555-0199

Attachments: OpenWeights_Master_Distribution_Terms_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karen Lee <karen@openweights.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Distribution & licensing for OpenWeights model family — partnership terms

Karen — thanks for the fast turnaround and the MPA. I ran this by the Partnerships and Product teams; a few clarifying items from engineering/legal that will influence our redline:

1) Hosted Serving License vs Redistribution:
   - We largely want to operate under the Hosted Serving License for hosted and Dedicated offerings. For Private deployments, we need an explicit statement allowing delivery of encrypted containers (or signed AMIs) to customer VPCs on a per-customer basis. That should not be treated as open redistribution to third parties.

2) Quantization & reconstitution risk:
   - Our inference stack performs post-training quantization and pruning. We can provide a technical attestation and a reproducible quantization recipe, but we will need explicit language that serving quantized artifacts under the Hosted Serving License does not imply permission to redistribute full-precision weights.

3) Revenue share / pricing:
   - 20% publisher baseline is reasonable for hosted API traffic. For Dedicated/Private we expect a blended model (smaller % on hosted, flat per-instance fee for Dedicated reservations, and a licensing fee for Private/on-prem). Can we get a rate card stub to use in contracting?

4) Compliance evidence:
   - Our SOC 2 and supply-chain controls will be shared with your legal team. If you have a vendor security questionnaire, please send it and we’ll prioritize it.

Next steps: Rishi (cc’d) will coordinate with engineering to produce the quantization attestation and an integration checklist. Aisha will coordinate a legal intro. We’ll send an internal redline to the MPA by Tue 10 Mar.

If that timeline works, can you also share any exclusivity restrictions (model-level or category-level)? We need clarity before committing to pilots with large customers.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-mpa-draft.docx (placeholder — internal note we’ll populate after legal review)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Looping in quick technical constraints from infra:
- We can support quantized-hosted inference with KV-cache and prefix-caching as long as the redistribution clause forbids shipping full-precision weights.
- For Dedicated pools, we need to know whether OpenWeights requires any specialized kernels or licensing per-GPU. If so, we’ll factor that into forecasting.
- Proposed deal id for tracking: OW-2026-028. Finance would like a stub revenue schedule to bake into the pilot MSA.

I’ll carve out time next Wed for a short sync with Karen + legal if that works.

—Rishi
Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Karen Lee <karen@openweights.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom@boldconsulting.com>, legal@openweights.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Distribution & licensing for OpenWeights model family — partnership terms

Thanks Marissa and Rishi — the MPA appendix covers most of what you asked. A few quick clarifications:

- Private/on-prem: we’re OK with encrypted container handoffs with a per-customer addendum; we’ll draft the addendum and include a list of required attestations (encryption keys handling, audit trail, handoff procedures).
- Quantization attestation: please include the exact quantization recipe. Our risk team will validate it; if there’s any residual reconstruction risk we may ask for a tighter obfuscation step.
- Exclusivity: we do not grant model-level exclusivity in the standard MPA. Category exclusivity can be negotiated for large-reseller agreements but requires minimum commitments.
- Rate card: attached a simple rate-card stub (commercial_terms_tab.xlsx) with hosted revenue share and Dedicated/licensing options.

Next step: I’ve uploaded a DocuSign envelope for an initial confidentiality & pilot SOW (link below). Please review with your legal team and we can schedule the legal + tech sync on Thu 12 Mar (Karen, Tom, Marissa, Rishi, Aisha).

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/NDYxMjM0

Karen
